title: Perfectly consistent 5x5 matrix (CR exactly 0)
description: A 5x5 matrix constructed as a_ij = w_i / w_j from the weight vector w = (16/31, 8/31, 4/31, 2/31, 1/31). Because the matrix is perfectly consistent, any correct implementation must return CR = 0 (to numerical precision), lambda_max = n, and the construction weights exactly; eigenvector and approximate prioritization methods coincide on consistent matrices.

source.citation: Constructed for this fixture set; see provenance fields.

scale.name: saaty-1-9
scale.notes: Judgments on Saaty's fundamental 1-9 scale; reciprocals (e.g. 1/3) and intermediate or fractional values are valid entries. Matrix entries may be given as numbers or as fraction strings such as "1/3".

ri_table.name: saaty

Saaty, 'The analytic hierarchy process - what it is and how it is used', Mathematical Modelling 9(3-5), 1987, p. 172 (average random consistency index, sample size 500), and as tabulated in J. A. Alonso and M. T. Lamata, 'Consistency in the analytic hierarchy process: a new approach', IJUFKS 14(4), 2006, Table 1 (Wharton column).

provenance.method: Constructed from a weight vector w by setting a_ij = w_i / w_j, which makes the matrix perfectly consistent by construction: the principal eigenvector equals w exactly, lambda_max = n exactly, and CI = CR = 0 exactly (not merely approximately). Every entry is an exact ratio of small integers. w = (16/31, 8/31, 4/31, 2/31, 1/31)
